hypothesis: Move from FM to a small MLP interaction model with DIN-style user-history attention while keeping the strongest ranking recipe found so far (BPR, recency prior, aux tasks, lower-lr schedule). The current best FM already uses mean-pooled positives, but pooled history is query-agnostic: every candidate for a user sees the same history vector. Within-user ranking should benefit if the user representation depends on the candidate item, because different impressions should attend to different past positives. The menu already exposes this as din_attention and requires an MLP-based model. DeepFM should also capture higher-order interactions among user/item/author/tab/history that FM cannot. This is a focused attempt to unlock extra nDCG@5 by improving top-of-list personalization while retaining the recency Bayesian prior as a low-variance memorization path.
